title: FlexSP: Accelerating Large Language Model Training via Flexible Sequence Parallelism
problem: Existing sequence parallelism methods for long-context LLM training assume homogeneous (equal-length) sequences and apply a single static scattering strategy, causing severe load imbalance when real training corpora have heterogeneous, long-tail sequence length distributions.
motivation: Long-context LLM training requires sequence parallelism across devices to handle sequences exceeding single-device memory, but the mismatch between static homogeneous scattering and real-world variable-length sequences wastes device utilization and increases training time.
method: FlexSP introduces flexible sequence parallelism that adapts the scattering strategy per-sequence to match each sequence's actual length. The system dynamically selects the degree of sequence parallelism and the scattering pattern (e.g., how many devices a sequence is split across) based on the length distribution of the current batch, balancing workload across devices and reducing idle time from length imbalance. Communication and attention computation are co-optimized under the flexible strategy.
key_novelty: Per-sequence adaptive scattering in sequence parallelism that dynamically matches parallelism degree to each input sequence's length, addressing the load imbalance caused by heterogeneous sequence lengths.
contributions: Analysis of load imbalance caused by applying static sequence parallelism to heterogeneous-length training corpora
FlexSP framework enabling flexible, per-sequence scattering strategies in sequence parallelism
Demonstration of training throughput improvements over static sequence parallelism baselines on long-tail length distributions

metrics.other: improved training throughput over static sequence parallelism (specific numbers not in abstract)

baselines: existing static sequence parallelism methods (e.g., Megatron-SP, DeepSpeed-Ulysses)
limitations: The adaptive scattering strategy may introduce additional scheduling overhead for highly variable-length batches; this trade-off is not quantified in the abstract.
primary_theme: Flexible sequence parallelism for heterogeneous-length LLM training
